LESSON: TRADITIONAL FORMS OF GOVERNMENT

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade six
Subject: General
Strand: POLITICAL SYSTEMS Strand Sub strand Specific Learning Outcomes Suggested Learnin
Topic 4.1: Traditional forms of Government
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 5

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Traditional forms of Government, part of POLITICAL SYSTEMS Strand Sub strand Specific Learning Outcomes Suggested Learnin in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade six General.

Key inquiry question: How were communities governed in the past?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. describe traditional forms of government of the Buganda and Nyamwezi in Eastern Africa,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Traditional forms of Government in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. compare traditional forms of government between the Buganda and Nyamwezi,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Traditional forms of Government in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. value aspects of good governance in traditional societies. Learner is guided to: ● brainstorm the traditional forms of government among The Buganda and The Nyamwezi of Eastern Africa, learners with speech difficulties could use alternative modes of communication to share their responses, ● draw a chart showing the governance structure among The Buganda and The Nyamwezi in Eastern Africa and display in class, learners with manipulation difficulties could use adapted drawing resources or be supported by peers or learner support assistant to draw and display their charts. How were communities governed in the past? 45 ● discuss the similarities and differences in traditional forms of government between The Buganda and The Nyamwezi, ● role-play scenarios depicting aspects of good governance in society, learners could be assigned roles according to individual ability levels during the role play.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Traditional forms of Government together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Self-Efficacy: Learners draw a chart showing the governance structure among The Buganda and The Nyamwezi in

Eastern Africa and display in class.

● Creativity and Imagination: Learners undertake tasks that encourage artistic expressions as they role-play scenarios

depicting aspects of good governance in society.

Values:
● Unity: Learners collaborate with others as they brainstorm the traditional forms of government in Eastern Africa (The

Buganda and The Nyamwezi).

● Responsibility: Learners find out the similarities and differences between selected traditional forms of government in Eastern

Africa.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

● Social Cohesion: Learners brainstorm, the traditional forms of government in Eastern Africa

(The Buganda and The Nyamwezi).

 Safety and Security: Learners interact with digital devices as they use digital or print resources to find out the

similarities and differences between selected traditional forms of government in Eastern Africa.

46

Link to other Learning Areas:

● Learners use Creative Arts skills to draw a chart showing the governance structure among The Buganda and The

Nyamwezi in Eastern Africa.

● Learners apply English/Kiswahili/KSL knowledge to role-play scenarios depicting aspects of good governance in society.

SECTION 6: SUMMARY

Main points to remember:

1. describe traditional forms of government of the Buganda and Nyamwezi in Eastern Africa,
2. compare traditional forms of government between the Buganda and Nyamwezi,
3. value aspects of good governance in traditional societies. Learner is guided to: ● brainstorm the traditional forms of government among The Buganda and The Nyamwezi of Eastern Africa, learners with speech difficulties could use alternative modes of communication to share their responses, ● draw a chart showing the governance structure among The Buganda and The Nyamwezi in Eastern Africa and display in class, learners with manipulation difficulties could use adapted drawing resources or be supported by peers or learner support assistant to draw and display their charts. How were communities governed in the past? 45 ● discuss the similarities and differences in traditional forms of government between The Buganda and The Nyamwezi, ● role-play scenarios depicting aspects of good governance in society, learners could be assigned roles according to individual ability levels during the role play.

Remember the key question: How were communities governed in the past?
